```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```


## Introduction 

This write-up describes how the metric Deprivation gap in early cancer diagnosis
is derived for the NHS Oversight Framework.

[NHS England » NHS Oversight Framework 2026/27](https://www.england.nhs.uk/long-read/nhs-oversight-framework-2026-27/)

To make sure we're all on the same page, here's some working definitions for
what we're talking about.

**Early cancer diagnosis** 

The proportion of cancers diagnosed at stage 1 and 2 out of all cancers
diagnosed at stages 1 to 4, observed over a 12-month period.

**Deprivation**

Uses Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) quintiles from 1 to 5, representing the
most deprived to least deprived areas in groups of 20%. These quintiles are
derived nationally, which makes it possible to compare across geographies, but
may mean some groups are over/under-represented in different areas.

**Deprivation Gap**

The difference in early diagnosis proportion between those in the most and least
deprived groups. That is, a measure of the relationship between deprivation and
the early diagnosis of cancer.

**Slope Index of Inequality** 

An SII is an absolute measure of inequality that represents the difference in
predicted values of an indicator between the most advantaged and most
disadvantaged subgroups, obtained by fitting a regression model, or line of best
fit. It is a standard method of measuring inequality in public health, used by
both Public Health England (PHE) and the World Health Organisation (WHO).

PHE: 
[Technical Guidance - Slope Index of Inequality](https://fingertips.phe.org.uk/static-reports/public-health-technical-guidance/Inequality/SII.html)

WHO Health Inequalities Handbook:
[Summary measures based on ordered inequality dimensions](https://whoequity.github.io/book_2024/4_analysis-reporting/Chapter21.html)

## How we measure the gap

We'll start with an example representing national early diagnosis by
deprivation.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true

example_df <- data.frame(
  deprivation_quintile = c("1 - most deprived", "2", "3", "4", "5 - least deprived"),
  ed_prop = c(0.555, 0.58, 0.595, 0.606, 0.619),
  ed_denom = c(39546, 43663, 48796, 51117, 50739)
)

example_df |> 
  transform(ed_prop = paste0(ed_prop * 100, "%")) |> 
  knitr::kable()
```

Visually, with the number of cases as the size of the points:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true

example_df |> 
  ggplot() + 
  aes(y = ed_prop, x = deprivation_quintile) +
  geom_point(aes(size = ed_denom)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0.55, .65)) +
  scale_size_continuous(limits = c(0, 55000), range = c(10, 12)) +
  labs(title = "Early Diagnosis Proportion by Deprivation",
       x = "Deprivation Quintile",
       y = "Early Diagnosis Proportion (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")  
```

### Quintile 5 minus Quintile 1

A simple and direct way to measure the distance between the extremes would be to
just take the difference between the early stage proportion in quintiles 1 and
5.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
gap <- example_df[5, "ed_prop"] - example_df[1, "ed_prop"]
```


$$
61.9\text{%} - 55.0\text{%} = 6.9 \text{pp}
$$

Note we measure this as a percentage point (pp) for a difference between
percentages. So we could say the least deprived quintile has 6.9 percentage
point higher chance of being diagnoses at an early stage than the most deprived
quintile.

However, a couple of potential issues stand out. Since the IMD quintiles are
derived nationally this gap makes sense nationally, but the number of cases in
each quintile for any one ICB may vary greatly.

### Building a line of best fit

```{r}
#| code-fold: true

example_df |> 
  ggplot() + 
  aes(y = ed_prop, x = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = ed_denom)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", 
              formula = y ~ x,
              se = FALSE, 
              fullrange = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0.55, .65)) +
  scale_size_continuous(limits = c(0, 55000), range = c(10, 12)) +
  labs(title = "Early Diagnosis Proportion by Deprivation",
       x = "Scaled Deprivation Quintile",
       y = "Early Diagnosis Proportion (%)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    breaks = c(0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")  
```
